transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, occupational health at my job sent me here. I run presses and do fabrication all day, and they're saying my weight is dangerously low for that kind of work. I don't really see it that way, though. I honestly just thought I was getting leaner and more disciplined.
When you look at yourself in the mirror or think about your body, do you ever feel afraid of gaining weight or see yourself as heavier than others tell you that you are?

I mean, yes, I definitely worry about gaining weight. It's just... if the scale goes up even a little bit, I panic. I start thinking that I'm going to lose all the control I've worked so hard for, and I just really don't want to end up heavy again. So I wouldn't say I see myself the way they do at work, I just see what I need to do to maintain my progress.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like a racing heart, feeling unusually hot, sweating more than normal, or trembling hands?

No, I haven't noticed any of that. My heart doesn't race, and I'm definitely not unusually hot. If anything, I'm usually freezing, especially out on the shop floor. But no sweating or trembling hands, nothing like that.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, so I can get a sense of your body mass index?

I'm about 5 foot 4. As for my weight, I'm not exactly sure what it is right this minute. I know what it was a few days ago, but I don't really want to get into the exact number. It's just... I know they think it's too low, but I don't.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, such as it becoming irregular or stopping altogether, since your weight has changed?
No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. It hasn't stopped or gotten irregular... it's just been normal, as far as I can tell.
The occupational health team must have recorded a weight when they referred you—would you be willing to share what that number was?

I'd really rather not say the exact number they wrote down. But... yeah, they recorded it. They actually sent me here from occupational health because they say my weight is dangerously low for someone running presses and doing fabrication all day. I just... I don't see it that way. I honestly thought I was just getting leaner, you know? Just being more disciplined.
Can you tell me approximately how much weight you believe you've lost over the past few months compared to what you used to weigh?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't... I haven't been keeping a running total or anything like that. I mean, I know I'm smaller than I used to be a few months ago, but I couldn't give you an exact number of pounds I've lost.
Would you be willing to step on the scale here in the office so I can get an accurate measurement of your current weight and height?
I'd really rather not do that. I know you want an exact number, but... I just don't want to be weighed right now. I'm not comfortable with it.
Can you walk me through what a typical day of eating looks like for you right now?

Well, on a normal day... I usually just have coffee before I head in for the early shift. Then, around lunch, I might have half a protein bar. After work, I usually do some yoga, and then I'll have a small bowl of vegetables. That's... that's pretty much it. If I eat more than that, I just feel like everything gets completely out of control.
Do you ever eat much more than you planned in a short period and then try to make up for it—like by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising intensely to 'undo' it?

No, I don't do that. I don't... I don't really ever eat large amounts like that in the first place. So I've never made myself throw up or used laxatives or anything to try and undo it. I just stick strictly to the small amounts I mentioned before. That's... that's how I keep things under control.
